summary: Completed the evidence-backed review of Carlisle Companies Incorporated common stock after the 2026-07-29 volume anomaly strengthened. The immutable CSL/XNYS/USD identity is unique and now linked to a maintained security page. The shares fell 7.78% over the measured month, and July 29 volume reached 1.108 million shares with a 2.70 z-score. The after-close Q2 release reported 8% revenue growth and 12% adjusted-EPS growth, but input and freight inflation reduced margins, first-half cash conversion was weak, and 2026 guidance now calls for flat adjusted EBITDA margin. A bounded 14x-18x normalized-EPS range gives 15.5% downside and 8.6% base upside. The medium-confidence assessment is baseline-comparison only; no conviction strategy or idea refresh was queued because the full strategy gate failed and neither the payload nor an accepted canonical relationship names an idea.

evidence.claim: Carlisle's current Q2 release confirms CSL common stock on the New York Stock Exchange and reports revenue of USD 1.570 billion, up 8%, operating income of USD 352.5 million, up 5%, and adjusted EPS of USD 7.03, up 12%. Adjusted EBITDA margin declined 70 basis points to 26.2% as petroleum-derived input and freight costs outpaced pricing. First-half operating cash flow was USD 197 million and free cash flow was USD 130 million. At June 30 cash was USD 665.3 million and long-term debt including current maturities was USD 2.890 billion. Management raised revenue guidance to mid-single-digit growth, changed the margin outlook to flat adjusted EBITDA margin, and increased the 2026 repurchase target to USD 1.2 billion.

Carlisle's FY2025 release reports revenue of USD 5.020 billion, adjusted EBITDA of USD 1.225 billion at a 24.4% margin, adjusted EPS of USD 19.40, operating cash flow of USD 1.1 billion, and free cash flow from continuing operations of USD 972 million. It identifies re-roofing as approximately 70% of commercial roofing demand while describing continued softness in new-construction markets.
